# Atomic Model **Stable orbits emerge — no electron shells, no quantum numbers.** Particles collide and merge into stable bound structures that persist for thousands of ticks. There are no electron shells, no principal quantum numbers, no Bohr radius — only leaf Frames making local greedy choices and the single-occupancy collision rule. **Why this is impossible (classically):** Stable atomic orbits require quantized energy levels — continuous mechanics predicts spiral decay (the classical electron should radiate and crash into the nucleus). Here the bound structures stay stable because the discrete 1-pixel-per-tick rule and emergent momentum conservation forbid the spiral. The scene is **real, editable user code**: the module cell `./setups/atomic-model.js` holds the shipped sketch file `lib/frqtl/scenes/atomic-model.js` verbatim — the SAME scene the GYM plays. Its first statement creates the 600x600 world (`exp.createCanvas`); then it builds the quarks, the proton and atom frame hierarchy and the orbiting electron from `Frame`/`Charge`/`Rectangle`. The **canvas cell** below DECLARES that module as a recipe (`setup="./setups/atomic-model.js" shape="recipe"`); the shim builds a recipe context and runs it. Nothing runs on load — click **Run** on the canvas (or **Run All**). *New to FRQTL? Start with **Hello, FRQTL** (`getting-started-hello-frqtl`) for the `caps.frqtl` setup-module + declarative-canvas basics this notebook assumes.* **Edit the physics:** open the `./setups/atomic-model.js` tab, change one of the scene's constants — e.g. `var QUARKS_PER_PROTON = 48;` → `12` — and re-Run. The emergent bound structure changes because you edited the construction, not a label. /* Copyright 2023-2026 by Essam Abadir */ /** * SCENE — Atomic model * * A sketch file: the WHOLE scene as one `export default function buildExperiment(exp)` module. The * world and the three-level frame hierarchy are built here from the engine's own primitives (leaf * frames — `engine().Frame`, read when the scene builds — and parent frames from a rect). Registered by * lib/shim/registry/walkthrough.js (rung atomic-model). * * Physics (zero new — bench H1, A1, A2, M1, M4): 48 one-pixel quarks fill an 8x8 proton frame; the * proton and one electron sit in a 64x64 atom frame. There is no force equation. Each parent's * compress() pulls its children one pixel toward its centre each tick (A1: a stationary parent * CONFINES a child), a parent's motion is carried by its children (A2), a parent's mass is its * child count (H1), and its wavelength is capacity/mass (M4) — 64/48 → the proton's oscillation. * The atom is stationary: the lab frame. `bonding` (noEscape) traps each quark in its parent's * live rect, so the nucleus holds together: binding emerges from compress, not from a law. * * Order (it seeds the run): world → the three layers → quarks (grid-filled, registered) → proton * from its rect → electron (registered) → atom from its rect → electron into the atom. */ import { Rectangle } from '@descix/frqtl-web/parts'; import * as OrbitBag from '@descix/frqtl-web/compat/renderer/orbit-bag.js'; import { engine } from '@descix/frqtl-web/compat/engine.js'; export const parts = {}; export default function buildExperiment(exp) { var W = 600, H = 600; // THE WORLD this scene states (its co-init call below) var QUARK_LAYER = 0; // 1x1 leaves var SUBATOMIC_LAYER = 3; // the proton: 8x8, capacity 64 var ATOM_LAYER = 6; // the atom: 64x64, capacity 4096 var QUARKS_PER_PROTON = 48; // the proton's mass at t=0 → wavelength 64/48 // ── WORLD — a 2D canvas + universe: quark layer fundamental, λ multiplier 1, quarks confined ── exp.createCanvas(W, H, { dimension: QUARK_LAYER, wavelengthScale: 1, bonding: true }); exp.declare(parts); var u = exp.universe; var quarkDim = u.addDimension(QUARK_LAYER); var subatomicDim = u.addDimension(SUBATOMIC_LAYER); var atomDim = u.addDimension(ATOM_LAYER); var subatomicW = subatomicDim.mb_w, atomW = atomDim.mb_w; var Frame = engine().Frame, Charge = engine().Charge; // the engine's own frame primitive + charge ABI var cx = Math.round(W / 2), cy = Math.round(H / 2); var atomRect = new Rectangle(cx, cy, atomW, atomW, null, true); var protonRect = new Rectangle(cx, cy, subatomicW, subatomicW, null, true); var rect = exp.runner.canvas_rect; // ── QUARKS — fill the proton rect column by column ───────────────────── var quarkW = Math.max(1, Math.pow(2, QUARK_LAYER)); var quarks = []; for (var x = protonRect.left; x < protonRect.left + protonRect.w && quarks.length < QUARKS_PER_PROTON; x += quarkW) { for (var y = protonRect.top; y < protonRect.top + protonRect.h && quarks.length < QUARKS_PER_PROTON; y += quarkW) { var q = Frame.makeLeafFrame(x, y, QUARK_LAYER, 1, 0, 0, false, Charge.POSITIVE, rect); q.name = 'quark_' + quarks.length; quarks.push(q); } } for (var i = 0; i < quarks.length; i++) { quarkDim.addFrame(quarks[i]); } // ── PROTON — the parent frame of the quarks ──────────────────────────── var proton = subatomicDim.createFrameFromRect(protonRect, quarks, 0, 0); proton.name = 'proton'; // ── ELECTRON — one negative leaf, upper-right of the atom ────────────── var electron = Frame.makeLeafFrame(atomRect.left + Math.round(atomW * 0.75), atomRect.top + Math.round(atomW * 0.25), QUARK_LAYER, 1, 0, 0, false, Charge.NEGATIVE, rect); electron.name = 'electron'; quarkDim.addFrame(electron); // ── ATOM — stationary parent of the proton; the electron joins directly ─ var atom = atomDim.createFrameFromRect(atomRect, [proton], 0, 0, true, true); atom.name = 'atom'; atom.insert(electron); u.leafQuantaWidth = quarkW; u.brownianMotion = true; // ── VIEW — frame the atom (render only: the 2D camera's `distance` is the visible physics-px // height). The atom is 64 px in the world; at 1.5x its width it fills two thirds of the view, // so the proton, its quarks and the electron are individually legible. ───────────────────── var cam = exp.runner.cameraControl; var flat = !OrbitBag.hasAngularPose(cam); if (cam && typeof cam.setOrbit === 'function' && flat) { cam.setOrbit({ target: { x: cx, y: cy }, distance: Math.round(atomW * 1.5) }); } } ## What you are seeing A dense central structure (the "nucleus") forms as particles merge, with lighter quanta settling into persistent surrounding orbits rather than collapsing inward. The stability is emergent — no force law holds the orbit together. The simulation runs live in your browser on the compiled FRQTL (WASM) engine. The same scene runs in the GYM and in this notebook cell — here it is editable user code in the `./setups/atomic-model.js` tab, not an opaque system fetch.
